# Inside the Nōaḥ restoration: what the marks recover
The domain you're reading about exists because someone refused to let **Nōaḥ** stay *noah*.

Nōaḥ's mythology is the rewriting of the world. The flood does not merely punish; it resets. After the waters, the same commands given to Adam — be fruitful, multiply, have dominion — are spoken again, as if creation itself has been given a second draft. God sees that human wickedness is great on the earth and resolves to blot out living things.  But Noah finds favor because he is righteous and blameless in his generation.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Nōaḥ
- **ASCII form:** noah
- **Meaning:** "Builder of the ark"
- **Domain of influence:** Patriarch, Survivor
- **Pantheon:** Canaanite
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** נֹחַ
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 167 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

Strip **Nōaḥ** to *noah* and one piece of evidence vanishes:

- **o → ō** — Macron: long vowel: the vowel length the ASCII form cannot show.

None of these marks is decoration. Each one is a fact about how the name was spoken, and each one is checkable against the scholarly record the temple cites.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Nōaḥ** lives at [/sites/noah/](/sites/noah/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/noah/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/noah/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/noah/patterns/).

The restoration preserves more than the ASCII form can say — stress, length, or a letter the Latin keyboard lost — which places it in Tier-1: mechanically verifiable, information-rich.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Nōaḥ** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Disaster Resilience & Recovery** — The ark; preparedness that outlasts the flood.
- **Faith & Spiritual Organizations** — The one just man of his generation, builder of the ark; his covenant with the bow is scripture’s first.
- **Ancestry & Heritage Services** — The patriarch from whom all nations descend.

This is the part of the file that surprises people: a four-thousand-year-old name, mapping cleanly onto twenty-first-century trades. The patterns are not marketing — they are the same myths, read forward.
## In the Sacred Texts

The Canaanite tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Enūma Eliš](/texts/enuma-elish/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on, free to read, cross-linked back to the names they mention. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.
## The File Continues

This is one of 271 Restoration Files — a second dispatch from every flagship temple in the fleet. The temple's [first dispatch](/sites/noah/blog/) tells the founding story of the name; the [blog index](/blog/) holds the whole archive.
